The 23-year-old's biggest moment of the game came in the second quarter when he jumped in front of a pass from Colts quarterback Daniel Jones for an interception, returning it 92 yards for his first career defensive touchdown. Lane has now compiled 20 total tackles (10 solo) and four passes defensed, including Sunday's pick-six, over seven contests during the 2026 campaign.

injuries.shortComment: The Jaguars placed Murray (elbow) on their injured reserve list Tuesday.
injuries.longComment: It was already known Murray suffered a season-ending elbow injury during the first quarter of Sunday's game versus the Colts, so the move comes as no big surprise. In his absence, 2025 sixth-rounder Rayuan Lane could step into a starting role at safety for the rest of the year.

injuries.shortComment: Woods (neck) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets, Nate Taylor of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Woods will not play in Sunday's game as he continues to deal with a neck injury he sustained in the Chiefs' Week 8 loss to the Broncos. The rookie first-rounder is continuing to make progress in his recovery.

injuries.shortComment: Remigio (hip) has been deemed questionable to suit up against the Jets on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Remigio has dealt with a hip issue this week but was able to log full practice sessions Thursday and Friday. That likely means he's trending toward playing Sunday, though his availability isn't a certainty. Remigio has a key role in the return game for Kansas City but has played just two offensive snaps through seven games.

injuries.shortComment: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Friday that Delane (shoulder) will not play Sunday against the Jets, Nate Taylor of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Andy Reid added that the rookie Delane is "making progress" but isn't quite ready to make his return, marking the second straight game the 22-year-old will miss. Delane has 27 tackles (17 solo), five pass deflections, and one interception in five games this season.

injuries.shortComment: Kelce (ankle) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Kelce was deemed a limited participant Wednesday, but the tight end's full participation Thursday paves the way for him to be in uniform Sunday against the Jets. Over his last two games, the Chiefs' leader in catches and receiving yards has amassed nine catches (on 15 targets) for 111 yards with a TD, and as long as he stays healthy he'll merit weekly fantasy lineup consideration.

injuries.shortComment: Rice (hamstring/knee) practiced without limitations Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Rice is off the injury report Thursday after kicking off Week 9 prep with a limited session Wednesday. The oft-injured wide receiver has been limited to five appearances this season, one of which he left before recording a catch, but he has 20 catches for 243 yards and two touchdowns across the other four games. With Rice getting healthier, he could feast Sunday against a Jets defense that's allowing 30.7 points per game during an active three-game losing streak.

injuries.shortComment: Head coach Andy Reid said that Butker will remain the Chiefs' kicker for Sunday's game against the Jets, Nate Taylor of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Butker -- who has made 12 of his 18 field-goal attempts in seven games this season -- converted one of his two tries along with with all three point-after attempts in the Chiefs' Week 8 loss to the Broncos. Despite his recent accuracy issues, Butker will retain his kicking role this weekend, even though the Chiefs recently signed Justin Tucker to the practice squad.

injuries.shortComment: Allen caught two of three targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos.
injuries.longComment: The rookie wide receiver usurped Jalen Royals on the depth chart, operating as the clear WR3 behind Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy. Allen ran 22 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 44 dropbacks, but with both Rice and Worthy healthy alongside Travis Kelce and Kenneth Walker, there doesn't appear to be much juice to squeeze for Allen.

injuries.shortComment: Gray caught both of his targets for 15 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos.
injuries.longComment: The Chiefs' TE2 caught a four-yard score in the third quarter, his first touchdown of the season. Kansas City uses plenty of 12 personnel, deploying both Travis Kelce and Gray on offense, but Gray handles more of the blocking duties. On the season, he has 14 grabs for 173 yards and a touchdown. There isn't much meat on the bone here for fantasy purposes.

injuries.shortComment: Johnson carried the ball once for 15 yards and caught all five of his targets for 128 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos. He added 44 yards on his only kickoff return.
injuries.longComment: The rookie running back flashed his explosiveness on a 73-yard catch-and-run in the second quarter that produced Johnson's first career NFL touchdown. He came into Sunday with a 9-109-0 line on 11 targets through six games, and his six touches were firmly behind Kenneth Walker's 25, but Johnson's breakout performance can only encourage Andy Reid to find more ways to get the ball in his hands. Johnson will look to build on this effort in Week 9 against the Jets.

injuries.shortComment: Worthy caught three of six targets for 13 yards during Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos.
injuries.longComment: Worthy put together another disappointing performance, reeling in three passes while failing to exceed 15 receiving yards for the second straight game. The wide receiver operated in a more prominent role for a couple weeks with Rashee Rice sidelined with a hamstring injury, but Rice returned to action Sunday and caught seven of eight targets for 53 yards. Worthy will continue to be an unappealing fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 9 matchup with the Jets.

injuries.shortComment: Walker carried the ball 21 times for 69 yards and caught four of five targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos.
injuries.longComment: The star running back was held below 100 scrimmage yards for a second straight game, but Walker watched his rookie backup, Emmett Johnson, erupt for a 5-128-1 line on five targets and take his only carry for 15 yards. Walker is still the clear No. 1 in the Kansas City backfield, but Johnson may have earned more consistent work with Sunday's impressive effort -- touches which might come at Walker's expense. He'll head into a Week 9 meeting with the Jets second in the race for the NFL rushing crown with 770 yards, just behind Bijan Robinson's 780.

injuries.shortComment: Mahomes completed 30 of 41 passes for 321 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos. He added six rushing yards on two carries.
injuries.longComment: The two-time MVP threw a TD in each of the first three quarters, including a four-yard toss to Noah Gray in the third that gave Kansas City a 24-13 lead, but Mahomes got shut out of the end zone over the final 15 minutes as Denver staged a comeback. It was the second three-touchdown performance of the season for Mahomes as well as his second 300-yard effort, after he threw for 382 yards and three scores against the Colts in Week 2. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 9 against a Jets defense that's allowed three straight quarterbacks to produce at least three TDs against it.

injuries.shortComment: Nussmeier (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Denver, though he will be available as the team's emergency quarterback.
injuries.longComment: Nussmeier is inactive for another contest. However, the signal-caller will be available if Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields exit the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

injuries.shortComment: The Chiefs placed Sneed (knee) on injured reserve Saturday.
injuries.longComment: Sneed was initially given the questionable tag for Sunday's game against the Broncos. He's been able to play through a lingering knee issue, but his placement on IR indicates that the injury has gotten to the point that an extended absence is warranted for the seventh-year defensive back. Sneed will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Bills on Thursday, Nov. 26. Jaden Hicks, Jadon Canady, Kristian Fulton and Christian Roland-Wallace are all candidates to see more work in the secondary due to the absences of both Sneed and Mansoor Delane (shoulder) for Sunday's AFC West tilt.

injuries.shortComment: Moore (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Broncos.
injuries.longComment: The lack of an injury designation indicates that Moore has cleared the league's concussion protocol. He should reclaim his starting spot at right tackle while Joshua Ezeudu reverts to a depth role.

injuries.shortComment: The Chiefs designated Norman-Lott (knee) to return from injured reserve Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: Norman-Lott was limited in his return to practice Wednesday. He's in the final stages of his recovery from a torn ACL that he sustained in October of 2025. The Chiefs now have 21 days to activate Norman-Lott from the PUP list, otherwise he would be forced to miss the entire 2026 season.

injuries.shortComment: Conner finished Sunday's 20-3 loss to Seattle with seven tackles (two solo).
injuries.longComment: Conner was on the field for every single defensive snap for a second consecutive game following the Chiefs' Week 5 bye. He missed the first three games of the regular season due to a knee injury but has suited up for each of the team's last three contests, during which he has accumulated 17 tackles (nine solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defense.

injuries.shortComment: Williams finished Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks with 10 tackles (four solo) and one interception.
injuries.longComment: The second-year defensive back's 10 tackles were a career best, and his interception off Sam Darnold late in the second quarter was also the first of Williams' NFL career. Williams is up to 29 tackles (17 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and seven pass defenses (including one interception) through six regular-season games.

injuries.shortComment: Bolton registered 11 tackles (six solo) during the Chiefs' 20-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Bolton played all but one of the Chiefs' 69 defensive snaps during Sunday's loss, and he finished second on the team in tackles behind Drue Tranquill (12). Bolton has recorded double-digit stops in four of six regular-season games and is up to 59 tackles (29 solo) and two pass defenses on the year.

injuries.shortComment: Tranquill finished Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks with 12 tackles (four solo).
injuries.longComment: Tranquil led the Chiefs in combined tackles Sunday, and he was one of three Kansas City defenders to reach double-digit stops. He's logged at least seven tackles in each of the first six games of the regular season and is up to 48 tackles (22 solo), two pass defenses and one fumble recovery in 2026.

injuries.shortComment: Booker (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game in San Francisco, Paul Gutierrez of the Raiders' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Booker was limited in practice Wednesday, then sat out the sessions Thursday and Friday entirely. He's thus set to miss his first game of the campaign. Booker typically plays one-third to one-half of Las Vegas' defensive snaps, and Tonka Hemingway may be asked to log a bigger workload with Booker sidelined.

injuries.shortComment: Thornton (back) does not have a designation for Sunday's battle against San Francisco, Paul Gutierrez of the Raiders' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Thornton was activated from IR last Tuesday but was a healthy scratch Sunday versus the Jets. He picked up a back injury that resulted in a limited practice Thursday this week, but with a return to full participation Friday, the second-year wideout will be available to face the 49ers. However, it's unclear if he'll suit up Sunday given his healthy scratch last weekend.

injuries.shortComment: Porter (groin) is listed as questionable ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Porter continues to deal with the groin injury he suffered early in the first quarter of the Raiders' Week 8 win over the Jets. If the cornerback cannot suit up for Sunday's contest, Jermod McCoy or Hezekiah Masses will likely start at outside cornerback across from Eric Stokes.

injuries.shortComment: Dean recorded 12 total tackles (two solo) during Sunday's 38-33 victory against the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Dean was able to notch exactly 12 stops for the fourth game in a row and fifth time this season. The linebacker is out to a great start to his first campaign in Las Vegas, registering 80 total tackles (38 solo), including 1.5 sacks, while also adding an interception and three forced fumbles over eight contests so far.

injuries.shortComment: Chinn recorded 10 total tackles (four solo) and an interception during Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Chinn had quite a day in Week 8, finishing second on the team in takedowns while also jumping in front of a deep ball from Jets quarterback Geno Smith for the safety's first interception of the year. Chinn has now compiled 56 total tackles (38 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding two forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries and an interception over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

injuries.shortComment: White was signed by the Raiders on Thursday, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: White was released by the team Tuesday to make room for Carter Runyon (foot), who was activated off injured reserve. With Runyon now waived and potentially joining the Raiders' practice squad, White was re-signed. To date, the 27-year-old has had the best season of his career, amassing eight catches (19 targets) for 112 yards and three touchdowns.

injuries.shortComment: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said Wednesday that the breakdown in carries between Washington and Ashton Jeanty will be determined on a week-to-week basis, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Per Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com, Kubiak said that he "absolutely" believes that Jeanty can be a bell cow running back, but at least for the time being, he looks like he'll be part of a timeshare with Washington. Jeanty has seen his carry count drop or hold steady in each successive game since Week 1, culminating in the 2025 first-round pick logging just two carries in this past Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets, while Washington carried a career-high 25 times for 83 yards. The split in carries may not be quite as dramatic in weeks to come, but Washington appears to have earned himself a sizable piece of the pie while he's averaging 4.3 yards per tote to Jeanty's 3.1 mark through eight games. Jeanty remains the Raiders' clear cut top option on passing downs over Washington, who has recorded just three receptions for 11 yards on six targets so far this season.

injuries.shortComment: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said Wednesday that the breakdown in carries between Jeanty and Mike Washington will be determined on a week-to-week basis, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Jeanty is averaging just 3.1 yards per tote on the season and has seen his carry count gradually decline with each successive game. After rushing a season-high 23 times in a Week 1 win over the Dolphins, Jeanty logged just two carries (for nine yards) in this past Sunday's win over the Jets, while Washington handled 25 carries (for 83 yards). According to McFadden, Kubiak said that he believes Jeanty can "absolutely" be a bell cow running back, but the second-year player out of Boise State looks like he'll be part of a timeshare with Washington until his production on the ground improves. Jeanty is still locked in as the Raiders' clear top back on passing downs, as he ranks first or tied for first with all NFL running backs in targets (49), receptions (37), receiving yards (376) and receiving touchdowns (three).

injuries.shortComment: Bech finished without a target or touch in Sunday's 38-33 Week 8 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Bech returned from a four-game absence due to a forearm injury and logged a 40 percent offensive snap share, but he didn't get any looks from QB Kirk Cousins. In fact, Cousins didn't go to his wideout corps as a whole very often -- 16 of his 26 targets went to tight ends, and another four went to running back Ashton Jeanty. Bech will look to get back into the box score Sunday in a Week 9 matchup in San Francisco.

injuries.shortComment: Mendoza didn't play in Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: With Kirk Cousins helping orchestrate a second-half comeback, Mendoza stayed glued to the sideline for the third straight contest after playing 10 offensive snaps in Week 5 against New England. The Raiders are 4-4 with Cousins playing reasonably well to keep the team in the postseason mix. Mendoza figures to get his shot if/when the Raiders are eliminated from postseason contention.

injuries.shortComment: Gay converted his sole field-goal attempt and all five PATs in the Raiders' 38-33 win over the Jets on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Gay converted a 53-yard field goal with 27 seconds remaining in the contest to put the Raiders up five points. The kicker is now 18-for-20 on field-goal attempts and a perfect 19-for-19 on PATs over eight regular-season games in 2026.

injuries.shortComment: Tucker did not catch his only target Sunday in the Raiders' 38-33 Week 8 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Despite quarterback Kirk Cousins throwing for 247 yards, Tucker had only one ball thrown his way. In fact, only one Raiders wideout -- Jalen Nailor -- had a reception, as Cousins targeted tight ends on 16 of his 26 passes. Tucker had caught either four or five passes in each of his prior six games and collected at least 97 receiving yards in three of those contests, though he finished below 45 yards in the other three. It's notable that he logged a season-low 52 percent offensive snap share against the Jets, but he should be in for better days ahead, beginning with a Week 9 matchup in San Francisco.

injuries.shortComment: Mayer caught five of six targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Mayer's six targets were second on the team behind Brock Bowers' 10, and only Bowers (26) ran more routes than Mayer's 20 on Kirk Cousins' 27 dropbacks. The tight end has just one touchdown this season but has remained an integral part of Las Vegas' passing attack. He's already surpassed his 2025 catches and yards totals, posting 36 grabs for 351 yards through eight games this season. Mayer will be a fantasy TE2 for next Sunday's date with the 49ers.

injuries.shortComment: Nailor caught all four targets for 38 yards in Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Both the catches and yards marked new season highs for Nailor, who entered Sunday with eight grabs for 75 yards and no touchdowns across six games. No team uses its receivers less than the Raiders, and Nailor accounted for four of the five targets between him and Tre Tucker against the Jets. Nailor has minimal fantasy appeal headed into next Sunday's road date with the 49ers.

injuries.shortComment: Cousins completed 19 of 26 passes for 247 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets. He added five rushing attempts for three yards and a rushing touchdown.
injuries.longComment: Cousins connected with Brock Bowers for touchdowns of 12 and two yards before scoring on a QB sneak in the third quarter for the 38-year-old QB's first rushing TD of the season and second rushing score since the start of the 2023 regular season. Cousins added a go-ahead two-yard touchdown pass to Jalen Nailor in the fourth quarter to take a 35-30 lead with 11:33 remaining. This was Cousins' fourth three-touchdown passing performance of the season but first since Week 4. All four of those three-TD outings came in Vegas wins, and Cousins has added seven touchdown passes in the Raiders' four losses to bring his TD:INT to 19:5 heading into a Week 9 trip to San Francisco.

injuries.shortComment: Bowers caught seven of 10 targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets.
injuries.longComment: Bowers scored a 12-yard touchdown in the first quarter and added a two-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter. He came just short of a third touchdown later in the third quarter, getting tackled just outside the goal line to set up a one-yard Kirk Cousins rushing TD. Bowers became the first tight end in NFL history to record at least 70 receiving yards in six consecutive appearances to begin a season. He'll try to extend his historic streak in Week 9 against the 49ers while continuing to work as the top target for Kirk Cousins.

injuries.shortComment: Shelley (ankle) has no designation for Sunday's tilt against the Texans.
injuries.longComment: Shelley missed each of Los Angeles' past three games while tending to an ankle injury. However, he followed two limited practices to begin this week with a full session Friday to position himself for a return Sunday. Shelley has played a rotational role in the secondary when active this season while also contributing on special teams.

injuries.shortComment: Perryman (undisclosed) has been deemed doubtful to suit up against Houston on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Perryman has been on IR all season due to an undisclosed issue. He was designated to return to practice Wednesday, and the veteran linebacker ended up logging a trio of limited sessions. However, it appears he's not quite ready to return to game action. In order for Perryman to have any chance to play Sunday, he'd need to be activated from IR on Saturday.

injuries.shortComment: Williamson (calf) has been ruled out for Sunday's matchup versus the Texans.
injuries.longComment: Willamson didn't practice at all this week, so he presumably picked up the calf injury in last Sunday's loss to the Rams. He's played exclusively on special teams this season, so Williamson's absence shouldn't affect the Chargers' defensive rotations.

injuries.shortComment: Leonard (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's Week 9 clash against Houston.
injuries.longComment: Leonard is presumably still in concussion protocol, though he was able to log limited practice sessions Thursday and Friday. Donte Jackson (hamstring) is returning from a three-game absence Sunday, so the Chargers will get a boost in their secondary despite Leonard's continued absence.

injuries.shortComment: Jackson (hamstring) does not have a designation for Sunday's tilt against the Texans.
injuries.longComment: Jackson missed each of the Chargers' past three games due to a hamstring injury, but he was able to log a full practice session Friday and is set to return to action against Houston. Before getting hurt, he started in three of his four appearances to begin the season, so he'll likely return to that role Sunday, especially since fellow cornerback Deane Leonard (concussion) has been ruled out.

injuries.shortComment: Thompson (quadriceps/hamstring) is officially listed as doubtful for Sunday's game versus the Texans.
injuries.longComment: Thompson was not able to practice at all during the week as he continued to nurse quad and hamstring injuries, and it appears likely he'll be absent for his sixth straight game in Week 9. Unless he's able to make a surprise turnaround by Sunday, Derius Davis figures to continue to see a few extra reps at wide receiver.

injuries.shortComment: Njoku (fibula) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Texans.
injuries.longComment: Njoku returned to practice this week but never advanced from limited participation to full. He could have a real shot next week when the Chargers face the Ravens. In the meantime, Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will get most of the TE snaps for Los Angeles.

injuries.shortComment: doubtful
injuries.longComment: doubtful

injuries.shortComment: Henley (shoulder) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
injuries.longComment: Henley was dinged up in Sunday's loss to the Rams but was able to return to the contest, and it appears he'll all set for the Week 9 tilt against the Texans. Henley has posted 41 tackles (17 solo), including 0.5 sacks, two fumble recoveries, a forced fumble and one pass breakup across seven starts this season.

injuries.shortComment: Lambert-Smith did not garner a target during Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
injuries.longComment: Lambert-Smith was expected to revert back to a minimal role on offense in Week 8 due to both Ladd McConkey and Tre' Harris returning to action, and that is exactly what happened. Lambert-Smith played just two offensive snaps in the contest, and he will continue to have little to no fantasy value as long as the rest of the Chargers' primary pass catchers are healthy.

injuries.shortComment: Kolar caught one of four targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
injuries.longComment: The tight end's four targets tied for third on the team, as he ran 17 routes on Justin Herbert's 37 dropbacks against Los Angeles. More of a blocker than receiver, Kolar has been forced to catch more passes out of necessity at times this season. He has 10 grabs for 98 yards on 17 targets. The catches and targets are both career highs in his fifth season.

injuries.shortComment: Harris caught all three of his targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
injuries.longComment: After missing Week 6 with a hamstring injury, Harris was healthy coming out of the Week 7 bye but played pretty clearly behind both Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston against the Rams. Harris ran just 20 routes to McConkey's 34 and Johnston's 30. Harris would see a big boost if Johnston gets traded ahead of next week's deadline.

injuries.shortComment: Mitchell rushed four times for six yards and caught all three of his targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
injuries.longComment: Handpicked by first-year OC Mike McDaniel as a free-agent signing in the offseason, Mitchell has been a total non-factor for much of the first half of the season. With a career 5.7 yards per carry average, Mitchell is averaging just 3.7 yards per rush this season. Involved in a three-way backfield committee with Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal, Mitchell is waiver-wire fodder in normal-sized 12-team fantasy leagues.

injuries.shortComment: Dicker made all three of his field-goal attempts during Sunday's 24-9 loss against the Rams. He did not kick any extra-point tries.
injuries.longComment: The Chargers offense put forth another poor effort in Week 8, with four of their 11 drives ending in punts and another three ending with turnovers. Dicker has mostly been efficient through his first seven games of the season, making 12 of his 14 field-goal attempts, but until the offense demonstrates it can consistently move the ball down the field, he'll be hard to trust as a fantasy option.

injuries.shortComment: Vidal rushed eight times for 23 yards and caught both of his targets for seven yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
injuries.longComment: The Chargers continue to use a fantasy-unfriendly three-man backfield, giving all three of Vidal, Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell meaningful touches and snaps. In a broken Los Angeles offense and crowded group of RBs, Vidal has minimal fantasy appeal outside of deeper formats.

injuries.shortComment: Johnston caught all four of his targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
injuries.longComment: Johnston's four grabs marked a new personal single-game high through six games this season. One of the least efficient wideouts in the league, Johnston entered Sunday with just eight grabs for 165 yards on 22 targets. He hasn't been playable in fantasy football for weeks and will square off with a stingy Houston secondary in Week 9.

injuries.shortComment: Gadsden caught all five of his targets for 52 yards during Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
injuries.longComment: Gadsden was able to lead the team in catches while he finished with one fewer target than team leader Ladd McConkey. The tight end has now reeled in at least three passes for the second straight game and third time over the last four contests after having failed to do so in any of the team's first three regular-season games. Gadsden and the rest of the Chargers will face a tough test in Week 9 against the Texans.

injuries.shortComment: Hampton rushed nine times for 20 yards and brought in two of three targets for seven yards in the Chargers' 24-9 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Hampton logged just one more carry than Kimani Vidal and five more than Keaton Mitchell, as the Chargers' ground game continued to resemble a committee scenario. Hampton now has 45 rushing yards or fewer in four straight games, and he's logged single-digit carries in three of those contests. The second-year back is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry behind an injury-hampered offensive line as well, leaving his outlook bleak for a Week 9 home matchup against an aggressive Texans defense next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: McConkey brought in four of six targets for 86 yards in the Chargers' 24-9 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: McConkey finally shook off the concussion that led to his exit from a Week 6 loss to the Chiefs during Week 8 prep, and despite the fact Tre' Harris also was back from a hamstring injury, the former still led the Chargers in receiving yards and targets. The yardage tally was also a season high for McConkey, who is averaging a career-best 16.8 YPC on his 17 catches to date. Los Angeles' air attack showed some improvement Sunday following some retooling during the Week 7 bye, and McConkey figures to remain the top target on the winless Bolts in a Week 9 home matchup against the Texans next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Herbert completed 24 of 32 passes for 257 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions while rushing four times for 15 yards in the Chargers' 24-9 loss to the Rams on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that remained with the Chargers.
injuries.longComment: The Chargers declined to move on from offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel during the Week 7 bye, and Herbert did finish with a season-high passing yardage total on a season-best 75.0 percent completion rate. However, Herbert failed to throw a touchdown pass for the second straight game while tossing multiple interceptions for the third time this season. Herbert still has just a 61.8 percent completion rate -- a career low by a fairly wide margin -- and a 5:10 TD:INT through seven games as the winless Bolts try again for their first victory in a Week 9 home matchup against the Texans next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: The Chargers placed James (hamstring) on injured reserve Saturday.
injuries.longComment: James missed the Chargers' three games prior to the Week 7 bye due to a hamstring injury. He suffered a setback in his recovery during Week 8 prep, which will require a stint on IR for the veteran safety. James is required to be sidelined for at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 29. Tony Jefferson will continue to operate in an elevated role in the secondary in James' absence.

injuries.shortComment: Alt (neck) was not listed on the Chargers' official injury report Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: Alt missed the Chargers' last two games before their bye in Week 7 because of a neck injury he suffered back in Week 4 at Seattle, but he is now on track to play Sunday against the Rams. He should start at one of the Chargers' tackle spots opposite rookie fourth-rounder Travis Burke in Week 8.

injuries.shortComment: Rivers (calf) does not have a designation for Sunday's clash against the Commanders, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Rivers suffered a calf injury against the Giants in Week 2 and was placed on IR soon thereafter. He was designated to return to practice this Wednesday and logged a trio of full sessions. Rivers' lack of a designation for Sunday's game suggests he has a legitimate chance of playing, but Los Angeles would need to activate him from injured reserve Saturday in order for that to happen.

injuries.shortComment: Whittington (back) is questionable for Sunday's matchup against Washington, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Whittington logged a trio of limited practices this week while managing a back injury. It might not be known if he'll be able to play Sunday until inactives are announced approximately 90 minutes ahead of the start of the game. Whittington has just two catches through seven games this season, but he also returns kicks and could work his way up to more responsibilities on offense with Davante Adams (hamstring) on IR.

injuries.shortComment: Ferguson (ankle) was expected to return for Sunday's game against Washington, but he's been ruled out after injuring his hamstring during Friday's practice, Cameron DaSilva of USA Today reports.
injuries.longComment: Ferguson made it back from his ankle injury, only to be sidelined by another concern two days before he was set for a return to game action. The Rams could use him, as they haven't found a second consistent receiving threat alongside Puka Nacua in the absence of Davante Adams (IR - hamstring). Another absence for Ferguson leaves Tyler Higbee as well as  Colby Parkinson (ribs, questionable), if available, as the Rams' tight top ends, with Davis Allen and Max Klare providing extra bodies for multi-TE sets.

injuries.shortComment: Garrett (knee) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Commanders, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
injuries.longComment: Garrett didn't practice Friday, but the Rams are planning to activate him from injured reserve Saturday, allowing the veteran edge rusher to play in Week 9. It will be a much-needed boost to the Rams' inferior pass rush.

injuries.shortComment: Parkinson (ribs) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Commanders, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
injuries.longComment: The veteran tight end managed to get in a limited practice Friday, keeping the door open for him to play after missing last Sunday's game against the Chargers. Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was initially slated to return to action this week, but was subsequently ruled out, so the status of Parkinson -- who has caught five passes in each of the last two games he played -- is worth monitoring.

injuries.shortComment: doubtful
injuries.longComment: doubtful

injuries.shortComment: Curl (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Commanders, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Curl did not participate in practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a foot injury likely suffered at some point in the Rams' Week 9 win over the Chargers. With cornerbacks Trent McDuffie (back) questionable and Jaylen Watson (shoulder) ruled out, Los Angeles' secondary could be short on a few key pieces.

injuries.shortComment: McDuffie (back) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Commanders, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Trent McDuffie was not seen at practice Friday, per Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com, marking him as a DNP for three straight practices ahead of Week 9. The 26-year-old tweaked his back in Week 8, in his first game back from a groin injury that kept him out for two weeks. With Jaylen Watson (shoulder) already ruled out for Sunday, the Rams could be short in the secondary against the Commanders.

injuries.shortComment: Lake recorded seven total tackles (two solo) and two passes defensed, including an interception, during Sunday's 24-9 win over the Chargers.
injuries.longComment: Lake was able to secure exactly seven takedowns for the third straight week, as he has now registered six or more tackles in every game this season. The 27-year-old's biggest moment of the contest came in the first quarter, when he jumped in front of a short pass from Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert for his third interception of the year. Lake has now compiled 56 total tackles (34 solo), a forced fumble, and 11 passes defensed, three of which are interceptions, over eight games so far in the regular season.

injuries.shortComment: The Rams signed Karty to their active roster Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Karty was elevated from the practice squad for each of the Rams' previous two games and handled kickoff duties while Brandon McManus kicked field goals and extra points. That arrangement isn't expected to change moving forward, per Nate Adkins of The Athletic, so it would likely take a McManus slump or injury for Karty to get a shot at the fantasy-relevant aspects of the kicker position.

injuries.shortComment: Watson is expected to undergo shoulder surgery and to miss the remainder of the 2026 season, Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times reports.
injuries.longComment: Watson was forced out of Sunday's game versus the Chargers early by a shoulder injury, and it was apparently severe enough to prematurely end his season. He had been operating as one of the Rams' top defensive backs and actually led the team in snaps at cornerback through eight weeks, so losing him is a significant blow to the club. His absence figures to create additional opportunities on the boundary for Emmanuel Forbes the rest of the way.

injuries.shortComment: Stafford (right elbow) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Sarah Barshop of ESPN reports.
injuries.longComment: Stafford was seen leaving the locker room with his upper right arm wrapped in ice after this past Sunday's win against the Chargers. Head coach Sean McVay told Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register on Monday that Stafford has been tending to arm soreness, but the quarterback clarified the situation with Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times on Wednesday, stating that he's had his right arm wrapped in ice regularly this season. An uncapped session to begin Week 9 prep puts Stafford in the clear to continue to lead the Ram's offense Sunday in Washington.

injuries.shortComment: Higbee caught one of two targets for 14 yards against the Chargers in Sunday's 24-9 victory.
injuries.longComment: Higbee logged a hearty 83 percent offensive snap share, most among Rams tight ends. However, he got little attention from quarterback Matthew Stafford, recording just two targets. Higbee had a nice run in Weeks 3-5, when he logged 18 catches for 212 yards across the three-game span. However, since then he's posted just seven receptions for 50 yards across his subsequent three contests. As such, it's hard to trust Higbee on a week-to-week basis right now even with the Rams down multiple pass catchers in Davante Adams (hamstring - IR), Terrance Ferguson (ankle - IR) and Colby Parkinson (ribs).

injuries.shortComment: Connors (hand) was placed on IR on Tuesday, Blaine Grisak of SI.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Connors broke his hand in Sunday's win over the Chargers and is slated for surgery. He's worked as a core special-teamer this season but hasn't logged a snap on offense. As such, Connors' IR stint -- which will last at least four games -- isn't likely to cause any waves in fantasy.

injuries.shortComment: McManus converted his sole field-goal attempt and all three PATs in the Rams' 24-9 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: While Joshua Karty handled kickoffs for the Rams, McManus was entrusted with field goals and extra-point tries. The kicker's first field-goal attempt with his new team was a 30-yarder, so the veteran player has not yet been challenged as a Ram.

injuries.shortComment: Stuard is battling a hamstring injury, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Stuard picked up the injury during pregame warmups prior to Sunday's win over the Chargers and is currently considered week-to-week. Shaun Dolac could be in line for increased playing time in Stuard's absence.

injuries.shortComment: Corum rushed 11 times for 73 yards and a touchdown and failed to bring in his only target in the Rams' 24-9 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Corum led the Rams in rushing yards despite logging five fewer carries than Kyren Williams, and, like the latter, Corum was able to get into the end zone. Corum's score came early in the third quarter on a winding 23-yard run, his second in as many games. The third-year back now has double-digit carries in consecutive games for the second time this season, and he's averaging a career-best 5.2 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Commanders next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Williams rushed 16 times for 56 yards and a touchdown and brought in his sole target for three yards in the Rams' 24-9 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Williams had a difficult time finding running room against a game Chargers defense, but he salvaged his fantasy day with a one-yard touchdown run late in the second quarter. Williams has five of his six rushing scores on the season in the last four games, and he's still averaging a robust 4.9 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Commanders next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Nacua secured 11 of 12 targets for 80 yards and a touchdown in the Rams' 24-9 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Nacua unsurprisingly led the Rams across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets and did so by a wide margin. With Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) unavailable for the last two games, Nacua has drawn 22 total targets and scored twice, with Sunday's touchdown coming on an 18-yard catch-and-run in the latter portion of the third quarter. Nacua is being used in a shorter-area role than past seasons -- he's averaging a career-low 10.1 yards per catch -- but he'll remain an elite fantasy option in a Week 9 road matchup against the Commanders next Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Proctor (concussion) does not have a designation for Sunday's Week 9 matchup versus Detroit, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Proctor suffered a concussion Week 7 against the Jets and didn't play this past Sunday versus New England. However, he was a full participant in all three of Miami's practices this week and has cleared concussion protocol. Proctor is therefore set to reclaim his starting role at left guard.

injuries.shortComment: Herring (neck) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Lions, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Herring logged three consecutive limited practices during Week 9 prep. The defensive end is battling a neck injury he sustained in the Dolphins' Week 8 loss to the Patriots, but it is uncertain if he will be able to overcome the issue in time for Sunday's game.

injuries.shortComment: Kacmarek (hamstring) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus the Lions, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Kacmarek played through his lingering hamstring issue in Week 8 versus the Patriots, and after practicing in full Friday, it looks like he's good to go for Week 9 as well. He should continue to operate as the Dolphins' second option at tight end behind starter Greg Dulcich.

injuries.shortComment: Allen (quadriceps) is officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game versus the Lions, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Allen managed a full practice Friday after being limited Wednesday and Thursday, so he may be on the 'probable' end of the questionable designation going into the weekend. Jaylen Wright is also questionable for Week 9, leaving starter Ollie Gordon as the only sure thing in the Dolphins' backfield ahead of Sunday's contest.

injuries.shortComment: Wright (quad) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Lions, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Averaging just 1.9 yards per carry, Wright is unlikely to get more than a handful of touches off the bench if he's active this Sunday. Ollie Gordon has been dominating Miami's backfield work.

injuries.shortComment: Rodriguez notched eight tackles (two solo) and forced a fumble in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots.
injuries.longComment: Rodriguez fell three tackles shy of Jordyn Brooks' team-leading total as the Dolphins dropped to 1-6. The rookie second-round pick's 12 tackles over the past two games mark the most fallow two-game stretch of Rodriguez's young career in that category. He'll try to pick up the pace in Week 9 against the Lions.

injuries.shortComment: Brooks recorded 11 tackles (six solo) in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots.
injuries.longComment: Brooks led the Dolphins in tackles during the loss, which dropped Miami's record to 1-6. The 29-year-old linebacker has slowed down a bit after leading the NFL with 183 tackles (99 solo) during the 2025 regular season, though he's still averaging a respectable nine tackles per game in 2026. He could draw interest on the trade market from contending teams in search of help at linebacker.

injuries.shortComment: Baker (undisclosed) is not ready to return to practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
injuries.longComment: Baker has been on the reserve/PUP list since Aug. 31 after suffering an undisclosed injury in July. The cornerback is eligible to have his 21-day practice window opened and begin practicing at any point, but he doesn't appear to be healthy enough to do so yet.

injuries.shortComment: Gonzalez reverted to the Dolphins' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
injuries.longComment: Miami plans to continue using Gonzalez as its starting kicker in Week 9 against Detroit, but the Dolphins will have to use his last practice-squad elevation in order to do so, per David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel. Gonzalez is 2-for-3 on field-goal tries and 5-for-5 on extra-point attempts through two starts this season.

injuries.shortComment: Washington caught five of six targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-19 loss to New England.
injuries.longComment: The five grabs led the team on the afternoon, and Washington capped his performance with a one-yard TD from Malik Willis just before halftime. It was Washington's first score of the season in seven games, and he'll take a 31-329-1 line on 45 targets into a Week 9 meeting with the Lions.

injuries.shortComment: Coleman caught all three of his targets for 46 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots.
injuries.longComment: Coleman led the team in receiving yards while reeling in multiple passes for the second time this season. The wide receiver's biggest moment of the game came in the fourth quarter when he connected with quarterback Malik Willis for a 35-yard score with 2:04 remaining in regulation. Coleman hasn't been a consistent part of the team's offensive approach this season, catching eight of 21 targets for 82 yards and two scores over seven contests so far.

injuries.shortComment: Gordon carried the ball 19 times for 69 yards in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots. He failed to catch his only target.
injuries.longComment: For the first time since De'Von Achane (knee) went down in Week 3 and Gordon became Miami's lead back, the second-year player was held out of the end zone. Over the last four games, Gordon has amassed 360 rushing yards and three TDs on 71 totes (5.1 yards per carry), but he's added exactly zero receiving yards to his totals. Gordon will try to begin a new TD streak in Week 9 against the Lions.

injuries.shortComment: Willis completed 21 of 32 passes for 211 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 24-19 loss to New England. He gained two rushing yards on his only carry.
injuries.longComment: The 27-year-old QB hit Malik Washington for a one-yard score just before halftime to give the Dolphins a 13-3 lead, but Willis' 35-yard strike to Kevin Coleman late in the fourth quarter was too little, too late after the Patriots dominated the second half. After throwing just one touchdown over the first four games of the season, Willis has a 5:3 TD:INT in the last three contests while adding two scores on the ground. He'll likely need to be even more productive in Week 9 as he attempts to keep pace with Jared Goff and the Lions.

injuries.shortComment: Douglas caught four of six targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots.
injuries.longComment: In his second game back from a multi-week high-ankle sprain, Douglas led the team with 31 routes on Malik Willis' 36 dropbacks against New England. The rookie wideout's six targets tied Greg Dulcich and Malik Washington for the team lead on a day when Willis targeted nine different pass catchers. Through four games this season, Douglas has 13 grabs for 226 yards and two touchdowns on 19 targets. He's a low-volume, big-play threat on the outside for Miami, but Douglas will be in the mix as a streamer for next Sunday's date with a leaky Lions secondary.

injuries.shortComment: Dulcich caught four of six targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots.
injuries.longComment: Dulcich has yet to score a touchdown this season, but the tight end is settling in as one of Malik Willis' favorite targets. He has at least four catches in four of his last five games but has reached 50 receiving yards in just two of seven contests. Dulcich is in the large bucket of low-floor, low-ceiling TE2 options in fantasy, but he does get a plus Week 9 draw against the Lions.

injuries.shortComment: Darrisaw (shoulder) was a full practice participant Friday.
injuries.longComment: Darrisaw began Week 9 prep with a limited session Thursday, but he was able to log a full session Friday. As such, he should be good to go for Monday's matchup against Buffalo.

injuries.shortComment: Claiborne (knee) did not participate in Friday's practice.
injuries.longComment: It is unclear where Claiborne sustained his knee injury, but the running back has downgraded to a DNP after being limited in Thursday's practice. The sixth-round rookie has been a healthy scratch since Jordan Mason returned from IR in Week 7 and will likely meet a similar fate in Week 9 regardless of any injury designation.

injuries.shortComment: Jennings (calf) did not participate in Friday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Jennings downgraded his practice participation Friday after being limited in Thursday's session. The wide receiver will likely need to show up in some capacity Saturday for a chance to suit up for Monday night's primetime showdown with the Bills.

injuries.shortComment: Van Ginkel (chest) was limited in Thursday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Van Ginkel played through the issue last week against the Lions and piled up 2.5 sacks in the loss. The veteran edge rusher has 21 tackles (11 solo), including 6.5 sacks, one interception, one forced fumble and a fumble recovery across seven games this season.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Brosmer is set to back up Carson Wentz against the Bills on Monday, as Kyler Murray (hamstring) won't play, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: It would likely take an injury to Wentz for Brosmer to get into the game, but the latter moves one step closer to getting on the field for the first time in 2026. Brosmer didn't look like an NFL-caliber QB as a rookie in 2025, posting a 0:4 TD:INT across seven appearances, including two starts.

injuries.shortComment: Murray likely won't play Monday against the Bills due to a hamstring strain, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Per head coach Kevin O'Connell, Murray is considered week-to-week, paving the way for Carson Wentz to make his second start of the season when the Vikings face the Bills on MNF. Per Lewis, O'Connell said Thursday that a stint on injured reserve isn't under consideration for Murray, suggesting that the starting quarterback's potential absence isn't expected to linger beyond 1-to-3 weeks.

injuries.shortComment: Wentz is stated to start Monday night's game against the Bills, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
injuries.longComment: Wentz will get the Week 9 assignment at QB for the Vikings, with Kyler Murray viewed as week-to-week with a hamstring strain, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. Max Brosmer will be the team's backup versus Buffalo, and perhaps longer than that should Murray's injury linger. Wentz thus represents an option for those in Superflex formats or otherwise are in need of signal-caller help due to injury or bye week issues.

injuries.shortComment: Dallas was signed to the Vikings' active roster Wednesday, Craig Peters of the team's official website reports.
injuries.longComment: Dallas will return to the active roster after playing in the first five contests of the year with the Vikings before being released and ultimately returning to the team as a member of the practice squad in late October. The running back has rushed four times for 14 yards and caught all four of his targets for 34 yards over seven contests with Minnesota this year, and he figures to operate in an extreme depth role behind Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason on Monday night versus Buffalo.

injuries.shortComment: Wilson registered 11 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, in Sunday's loss to Detroit.
injuries.longComment: Wilson finished second on the Vikings in stops, behind only Josh Metellus (13). One of his tackles was a sack of Jared Goff for a 10-yard loss on Detroit's first drive of the game, resulting in a Detroit punt. Wilson has 3.0 sacks through seven games, so he could surpass the career-best mark of 6.5 sacks he recorded over 17 regular-season games last year.

injuries.shortComment: Metellus recorded 13 tackles (six solo) and a defensed pass in a Week 8 defeat against Detroit.
injuries.longComment: Metellus led Minnesota in tackles and recorded a season-high mark in the process. He's been a consistent presence for the Vikings' tough defense this season, playing every defensive snap in six of the team's seven contests so far. Metellus is up to 50 stops through seven games, putting him on pace for the third triple-digit tackle campaign of his career.

injuries.shortComment: Murphy registered 10 tackles (eight solo) in a loss to the Lions on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Murphy tied for third on Minnesota in tackles on a day when four Vikings finished with double-digit stops. The tackle tally was Murphy's highest of the season and snapped a four-game stretch of posting three stops or fewer. The veteran cornerback is enjoying a nice campaign overall, as he's tallied three interceptions so far, tying for second in the NFL in that category.

injuries.shortComment: Cashman finished Sunday's loss to Detroit with 10 tackles (five solo).
injuries.longComment: Cashman was one of four Vikings to notch double-digit stops in the team's first loss of the season. The veteran linebacker has recorded at least seven stops in each of his seven games this season and has registered double-digit tackles three times. He's well beyond pace for a fourth consecutive season of triple-digit tackles, as he already has 64 stops (including 4.5 sacks) through seven contests.

injuries.shortComment: Reichard missed his sole field-goal attempt and made his sole PAT in the Vikings' 19-15 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Reichard missed a 57-yard field goal on the first drive of the game. The kicker's miss proved costly as the Vikings lost a four-point game that went down to the wire. Reichard is now 18-for-20 on field-goal attempts and 10-for-10 on PATs through seven regular-season games in 2026.

injuries.shortComment: Hockenson caught four of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions.
injuries.longComment: Hockenson secured an eight-yard touchdown midway through the fourth quarter to give the Vikings a 15-12 lead, and he's now up to 31 grabs for 295 yards and three touchdowns on 37 targets through seven games this season. Hockenson, though, missed all but two offensive snaps in the Week 5 win over the Saints after suffering a concussion. A favorite target for Kyler Murray in the middle and short areas of the field, Hockenson has settled in as a lower-end TE1 in fantasy. He gets a plus matchup with the Bills next Monday night in another spot the Minnesota offense may be forced to push the gas pedal.

injuries.shortComment: Addison caught three of eight targets for 66 yards in Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions.
injuries.longComment: Addison's big play was a 51-yard catch over the top of the defense in the fourth quarter to set the offense up at the 10-yard line. T.J. Hockenson scored a go-ahead touchdown two plays later. Addison's eight targets on the day were one fewer than Justin Jefferson, but it was the former who paced the team in receiving yards. Playing in a Minnesota offense that doesn't push the ball down the field much or focus on its outside receivers, Addison has just 16 catches for 249 yards and one touchdown on 33 targets through six games this season. He'll be a fantasy WR4 with upside next Monday night against a leaky Bills secondary.

injuries.shortComment: Jones rushed five times for 22 yards and brought in both targets for 18 yards in the Vikings' 19-15 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Jones shook off the knee injury that had knocked him out of a Week 7 win over the Colts to head into Sunday without a designation. However, the veteran finished with a season low in carries and rushing yards. Jones has just 13 combined rush attempts -- a number partly influenced by the aforementioned early exit against Indianapolis -- in the two games since Jordan Mason returned from injured reserve, and it remains to be seen if the modest role will persist in a Week 9 home matchup against the Bills on Monday night, Nov. 9.

injuries.shortComment: Mason rushed eight times for 20 yards in the Vikings' 19-15 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Playing in his second game since returning from an IR stint due to a thumb injury, Mason paced the Vikings' ground attack in carries but finished two yards behind Aaron Jones, who logged five totes. Mason also wasn't targeted for the second time in three games, and Minnesota's running game figures to continue in a fantasy-averse timeshare between the two. Mason will look to make inroads against what has been an improved Bills run defense in a Week 9 home showdown on Monday night, Nov. 9.

injuries.shortComment: Jefferson brought in five of nine targets for 33 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings' 19-15 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Jefferson led the Vikings in receptions with the aid of a team-high target total, and the highlight of the perennial Pro Bowler's afternoon was his touchdown grab. Jefferson stuck his hand up and tapped Kyler Murray's (hamstring) pass to himself while in tight coverage in the left corner of the end zone early in the second quarter, ultimately securing a memorable one-yard score. Jefferson has topped 50 receiving yards just three times and is still in search of his first 100-yard game of the season, but he's found the end zone in two of the last three games heading into a Week 9 home showdown against the Bills on Monday night, Nov. 9.

injuries.shortComment: Jacas (knee) does not have a designation for Sunday's contest versus Green Bay.
injuries.longComment: Jacas made an early exit Sunday versus Miami due to a knee issue. He was limited in the first two Patriots practices this week but was able to upgrade to full participation Friday, clearing the way for him to suit up Week 9.

injuries.shortComment: Hollins (calf) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Packers.
injuries.longComment: The Patriots would need to activate Hollins from injured reserve by 4 p.m. ET on Saturday to have him available for Sunday's game against the Packers. The team could certainly use him with A.J. Brown (knee) out again, but Hollins never made it back to full practice participation, instead logging limited sessions Wednesday through Friday.

injuries.shortComment: With TreVeyon Henderson (illness) ruled out for Week 9, Stevenson is set to handle an expanded workload Sunday against the Packers, Mark Daniels of MassLive.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Henderson will miss a second straight game tending to medical issue. With the second-year running back out last week against Miami, Stevenson logged 76.7 percent of the offensive snaps and handled a season-high 19 carries, turning them into 82 scoreless yards. He also caught three passes on three targets. Stevenson will be a volume-driven, home-favorite RB1/2 for fantasy against Green Bay, while Corey Kiner will step into the RB2 role again.

injuries.shortComment: Henderson (illness) won't play Sunday against the Packers, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Per Mark Daniels of MassLive.com, Mike Vrabel said that the Patriots won't put a timeline on Henderson's return, while adding, per Lazar, that the team is "just trying to make sure that TreVeyon is cared for and his recovery plan is intact and he's comfortable with it." In the absence of Henderson -- who recently experienced "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms" -- Rhamondre Stevenson will pace New England's backfield, with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison also mixing in.

injuries.shortComment: Henry (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Packers, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
injuries.longComment: After opening the week with back-to-back missed practices, Henry's designation leaves the door open for him to play heading into Sunday. If he can't play, New England would need to lean more heavily on rookie Eli Raridon at tight end against Green Bay.

injuries.shortComment: Brown (knee/ankle) remained sidelined at practice Friday, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
injuries.longComment: With three consecutive DNPs looming, Brown doesn't seem likely to be available Sunday against the Packers. If Brown is ruled out later Friday, the stage would be set for DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, Kyle Williams and potentially Mack Hollins (calf) -- who has been designated to return from IR -- to handle New England's Week 9 WR duties.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Van Roten (thigh) was designated to return from injured reserve by New England on Wednesday, Matt Legros of Patriots Wire reports.
injuries.longComment: Van Roten has been on injured reserve since Sept. 29 while recovering from a thigh injury, and the team opened his 21-day practice window. If the offensive lineman is unable to be activated in that time frame, he will be forced to remain on IR for the rest of the year.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Chism caught all five of his targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins.
injuries.longComment: Chism led the team in targets and receptions, with A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) unavailable. The wide receiver played a season-high 88 percent of the team's offensive snaps, and he has now reeled in 15 of 20 targets for 151 yards and a touchdown over seven regular-season contests with New England so far this year.

injuries.shortComment: Kiner rushed seven times for 38 yards during Sunday's 24-19 win over Miami.
injuries.longComment: Kiner operated as the top reserve option behind starting running back Rhamondre Stevenson in Week 8, with TreVeyon Henderson (illness) sidelined. Kiner has compiled 160 rushing yards on 28 carries while reeling in his only target for seven yards over the team's last four contests, and he could earn more opportunities moving forward.

injuries.shortComment: Bryant (ankle) was activated from injured reserve by the Patriots on Tuesday.
injuries.longComment: Bryant will return to action in Week 9 after spending the entirety of the regular season to this point on IR after suffering an ankle injury during the preseason. The 24-year-old will operate as a top reserve option behind Will Campbell and Morgan Moses at offensive tackle moving forward.

injuries.shortComment: Borregales made one of his two field goals and all three PATs in the Patriots' 24-19 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Borregales missed a 40-yard field goal during the Patriots' last drive of the first half. The kicker continues to struggle in the intermediate range, now sitting at 7-for-10 on field-goal attempts from 30-49 yards during the 2026 regular season.

injuries.shortComment: Raridon had one reception for five yards on four targets in New England's 24-19 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Raridon's lone reception went for five yards early in the first quarter. He didn't record another catch for the remainder of the contest despite logging a hefty 93 percent offensive snap share, largely due to No .1 tight end Hunter Henry departing in the first half due to a foot injury. Should Henry remain sidelined in Week 9, Raridon will have another big opportunity to produce in a home tilt against Green Bay.

injuries.shortComment: Williams caught his lone target for a 43-yard touchdown during Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins.
injuries.longComment: Williams made the most of his only touch in Week 8, scoring on a 43-yard deep ball from Drake Maye in the third quarter. The wide receiver had an opportunity to be more involved with A.J. Brown (knee) sidelined Sunday, but Williams saw just one target for the third game in a row. On the year, the wide receiver has now caught seven of 13 targets for 190 yards and two touchdowns over eight regular-season contests.

injuries.shortComment: Douglas caught all three of his targets for 76 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins.
injuries.longComment: Most of his production came on a nifty 48-yard catch-and-run in the fourth quarter, as Douglas took a strike from Drake Maye along the sideline but then curled back toward the middle of the field and dashed the remaining 30 yards to the end zone while out-racing four Miami defenders. It was the fourth touchdown of the season for the fourth-year wideout, a new career high, and Douglas will take a 26-332-4 line on 37 targets through eight games into a Week 9 tilt against the Packers.

injuries.shortComment: Maye completed 16 of 20 passes for 199 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins. He added five rushing yards and a TD on eight carries.
injuries.longComment: While he failed to reach 200 passing yards for the third time in eight games this season, Maye put together a very efficient performance as he produced multiple TDs for a fifth straight game. All three scores came in the second half as the QB rallied the Patriots from a 13-3 deficit, hitting Kyle Williams for a 43-yard score in the third quarter and DeMario Douglas for a 48-yard strike in the fourth, while running for a two-yard TD in between. Maye appears to have gotten his recklessness under control, committing just one turnover in the last four contests, and he'll take a 15:8 TD:INT on the season into a Week 9 clash with the Packers.

injuries.shortComment: Banks (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Browns.
injuries.longComment: Banks logged three consecutive limited sessions during Week 9 prep. The Saints could choose to activate the left tackle ahead of Sunday's game but will need to free up a 53-man roster spot to do so.

injuries.shortComment: Reid (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns.
injuries.longComment: Reid was a full participant in all three Week 9 practice sessions. The Saints' starting strong safety has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and is all set to suit up for Sunday's game against the Browns.

injuries.shortComment: Emerson (shin) is questionable to suit up for Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the Browns.
injuries.longComment: Emerson was a limited participant in each of New Orleans' first two practices this week due to a shin injury. However, he downgraded to non-participation Friday and was given a tag of questionable for Sunday. Should Emerson not be able to play against Cleveland, Quincy Riley would likely return to a starting role.

injuries.shortComment: Kamara (rest/back) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game versus the Browns.
injuries.longComment: Kamara went from DNP due to rest/back Wednesday to limited Thursday and finally full Friday, paving the way for him to be available to the Saints backfield. With fellow RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) sidelined this weekend, it'll be Kamara and Kendre Miller to handle the load Sunday.

injuries.shortComment: Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
injuries.longComment: With Donaldson out and Travis Etienne (hamstring) still on injured reserve, the Saints will roll with a three-man backfield of Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller and Audric Estime. One of the league's least productive backfields doesn't evoke much fantasy excitement.

injuries.shortComment: Tyson (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Browns, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: With Tyson having logged limited practices after the Saints opened his 21-day window to return from injured reserve Wednesday, Friday's designation gives the rookie a chance to make his long-awaited regular-season NFL debut. There's been no indication one way or the other on what the Saints' plans are for Tyson this week. Devaughn Vele and Bryce Lance would be the biggest losers in terms of playing time and targets once Tyson does debut.

injuries.shortComment: Ruiz (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
injuries.longComment: Ruiz missed the Saints' pre-bye game against the Steelers in Paris, but the two weeks off were apparently enough to get him ready for Week 9 against Cleveland.

injuries.shortComment: Shepherd (illness) practiced in full Wednesday.
injuries.longComment: Shepherd hasn't played since Week 4 but appears ready to return for Sunday's game against the Browns. He has 12 tackles (three solo), including 0.5 sacks, across 175 defensive snaps this season.

injuries.shortComment: questionable
injuries.longComment: questionable

injuries.shortComment: Coach Kellen Moore announced Wednesday that Smyth will be the Saints' kicker in Week 9, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Smythe will take over for the recently released Daniel Carlson. A native of Northern Ireland, Smythe went 12-for-16 on field goals over six games for the Saints in 2025.

injuries.shortComment: Head coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday that the Saints haven't opened Etienne's (hamstring) practice window just yet, Jeff Nowak of WWL Louisiana reports.
injuries.longComment: Etienne has missed the required four games on IR due to a strained left hamstring, but even with the benefit of a Week 8 bye, he hasn't gained clearance to mix into drills. Moore told Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana on Monday that Etienne has a chance to return to practice this week, but with no on-field work to begin Week 9 prep, he seems to be on the outside looking in to have enough time to be activated for Sunday's contest against the Browns.

injuries.shortComment: Granderson totaled four tackles, including 1.5 sacks, in Sunday's Week 7 loss to Pittsburgh.
injuries.longComment: Granderson helped keep the game close with a pair of key sacks. He brought down Aaron Rodgers near the end of the second quarter to help hold the Steelers to a field goal, then split a sack in the red zone at the end of the third period to again limit Pittsburgh to three points. Granderson is up to 5.5 sacks through six games on the campaign, giving him an excellent chance of surpassing the career-high mark of 8.5 sacks he established over 17 contests in 2023.

injuries.shortComment: Werner finished Sunday's loss to the Steelers with eight tackles (three solo).
injuries.longComment: Werner had a two-game streak of double-digit stops snapped, but he was still plenty productive. The veteran linebacker dealt with a neck injury in early October but appears past that issue, as he's played every Saints defensive snap in three straight contests. Werner leads New Orleans with 54 tackles (including 2.0 sacks) through seven games.

injuries.shortComment: Sanker posted nine tackles (seven solo) in Sunday's Week 7 loss to Pittsburgh.
injuries.longComment: Sanker recorded his second-highest tackle tally of the campaign to lead New Orleans in that category. The second-year defender has now tallied six or more stops in five of his seven games this season. With 44 tackles through seven contests, Sanker is easily on pace to surpass the 80 stops he notched in 17 games as a rookie.

injuries.shortComment: Fant gathered in all two targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 16-10 defeat against Pittsburgh.
injuries.longComment: After finding the end zone twice in the loss to the Raiders in Week 3, Fant has combined for just three catches in his previous three appearances. While his two receptions Sunday were a small step in the right direction, he is expected to continue to play second fiddle to Juwan Johnson moving forward. It may also be a matter of time before rookie Oscar Delp logs more snaps from week to week.

injuries.shortComment: Lance reeled in all two targets for 12 yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh.
injuries.longComment: Lance had two catches for the second consecutive game, though unlike the Week 6 win over the Giants, he didn't find the end zone. The 24-year-old has logged 332 offensive snaps this season, third in the receiving corps behind Chris Olave (387) and Devaughn Vele (438). However, despite being on the field more often than most of the other wideouts on the roster, Lance hasn't been productive thus far in his rookie campaign.

injuries.shortComment: Miller rushed eight times for six yards in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers in Paris.
injuries.longComment: The Saints got absolutely nothing going on the ground against Pittsburgh, rushing 17 times for 18 yards as a team, so it's not like Miller and his team-leading eight carries was the only issue. New Orleans heads into its bye in Week 8, and Travis Etienne (hamstring) will be eligible to come off injured reserve for Week 9 against the Browns. When both Etienne and Alvin Kamara were healthy and active together earlier this season, Miller was a healthy inactive.

injuries.shortComment: Brown hauled in all three targets for 57 yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
injuries.longComment: Brown had the most productive game of his NFL career thus far, catching more passes than he had in his previous five appearances combined. The 2026 No. 190 overall pick should continue to get consistent work on special teams. However, despite the recent uptick in offensive snaps, it's unknown if Brown will continue to be more involved as a pass catcher moving forward.

injuries.shortComment: Johnson caught one of three targets for seven yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
injuries.longComment: Johnson was held in check yet again in Week 7. The tight end has now gone three straight games without exceeding 16 receiving yards, and he hasn't scored a touchdown since Week 3. Johnson has slowly become an unreliable fantasy option as the season has progressed, but he'll have the opportunity to hit the reset button during the Saints' bye week in Week 8.

injuries.shortComment: Vele caught all five of his targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
injuries.longComment: The third-year wideout was on the other end of Tyler Shough's only TD pass of the day, hauling in a one-yard toss in the second quarter for the Saints' final points. Vele tied his career high with his third touchdown of the season, and his 33-348-3 line on 48 targets through seven games has him tracking toward a career-best campaign heading into a Week 8 bye. His role could shrink significantly after the bye, however, if rookie Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is cleared to make his NFL debut.

injuries.shortComment: Thomas (groin) does not have a designation for Sunday's matchup in Philadelphia.
injuries.longComment: A lingering groin issue held Thomas to limited practice sessions Wednesday and Thursday, but he was able to log a full session Friday to avoid a designation heading into the weekend. The star left tackle will therefore continue to anchor the offensive line for the first-place Giants.

injuries.shortComment: Nabers (knee) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Philadelphia.
injuries.longComment: Nabers was held out of drills Thursday due to a knee injury, but his return to all activity one day later lines up with head coach John Harbaugh's assessment of the situation Friday, when he told Matt Citak of the Giants' official site that the wide receiver "practiced fully" and is "full go" for Week 9. As a result, Nabers will look to build upon the massive 36-509-2 line on 51 targets that he's accrued over the last four contests.

injuries.shortComment: With Cam Skattebo (hamstring) doubtful to play Week 9, Singletary is expected to operate as the Giants' lead back Sunday against the Eagles, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports.
injuries.longComment: Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) is on injured reserve and required to miss at least the next four games, and Najee Harris was recently released, so it'll be Singletary's job Sunday. Practice-squad types Greg Desrosiers and Phil Mafah are in tow as the backups but both have little-to-no experience carrying the ball in the NFL. Volume alone will put Singletary in the fantasy RB2 mix.

injuries.shortComment: Skattebo (hamstring) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
injuries.longComment: Skattebo was able to manage one limited practice (Friday) this week, and while head coach John Harbaugh told Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post that the Giants are "keeping the door open" for the running back to play in Week 9, his official listing implies it's more likely just ajar. In any case, if Skattebo ends up sitting out Sunday, Devin Singletary likely will serve as New York's lead runner, with Greg Desrosiers and potentially practice-squad members Eric Gray and Phil Mafah in line for work behind him.

injuries.shortComment: Desrosiers could serve as a potential backup for the Giants on Sunday, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
injuries.longComment: Desrosiers is listed as running back No. 3 on the Giants' depth chart and could be in line to back up Devin Singletary on Sunday if Cam Skattebo can't play after being listed as questionable with a hamstring injury. Desrosiers has yet to play in a regular-season game this season. In three preseason games, he rushed 23 times for 166 yards and a touchdown.
